messages:
Ella: Quick intake — we need a short PRD for 'customer rollout controls' requested by FinanceApp and RetailCo. Problem: customers want server-side controls to pin rollout %, require rollout approval gates, and define per-customer acceptance metrics. This is blocking Dedicated contracts for both customers.

Raj: TL;DR of ask?

Ella: They want two things: 1) ability to schedule/limit % of traffic to a new model per-customer, and 2) acceptance criteria that, if failing, auto-rolls back or notifies.

Tess: Are we talking UI + API? Or just API first?

Ella: API-first preferred. UI optional for GA. Product goal is to unblock enterprise signups, not to build full console flow now.

Kevin: Ops question — what SLOs are they tying acceptance to? latency, error rate, or quality metrics?

Maria: FinanceApp cares about quality (semantic accuracy) and latency tail. RetailCo cares mainly about cost and failed prompts.

Raj: Suggest we split into MVP vs stretch: MVP = per-customer rollout percentage + manual rollback + simple acceptance hooks (latency, error rate). Stretch = automated rollback on quality regressions using eval sets.

Ella: Good framing. Add problem statement to the PRD: customers need deterministic control of exposure to new models while being able to define safety nets. Non-goal: not building closed-loop quality training or model retraining.

Tess: Engineering constraints: our routing layer supports global rollout %, but not per-customer. We'll need to add routing keys on customer_id and push policy changes down the control plane. Work estimate? 2 sprints backend, 1 sprint frontend (if UI).

Kevin: Observability: we need per-customer metrics (p95 latency, 5xx rate, token cost) emitting to console + alerts. Otherwise auto-rollback can't be reliable. Ops-bot: suggest alerting thresholds + runbook.

ops-bot: https://intranet.redwood/practices/rollout-runbook — recommend using alert group 'rollout-violations' and service tag 'routing'.

Raj: Acceptance criteria draft (MVP):
- API: POST /rollouts {customer_id, model_id, percent, start_ts, end_ts, acceptance: {metrics}} returns rollout_id
- Routing respects per-customer percent within 5% of configured value under normal load
- Manual rollback via DELETE /rollouts/{id} within 30s
- Metrics emitted per customer for p50/p95 latency, 5xx rate, token_cost per request
- Alerts trigger if p95 > configured or 5xx rate increases by >0.5% absolute over baseline

Ella: Success metrics (business):
- Close at least 2 Enterprise dedicated deals that were stalled for this feature within 60 days of GA
- <2 customer-reported incidents related to rollouts in first 90 days

Tess: Edge cases to capture in PRD:
- Customer with multiple routing keys (org-level + team-level) — which wins?
- Overlapping rollouts (two models with same percent) — expected behavior: highest priority wins or last-write?
- Low-traffic customers where percent math rounds to 0 — should support minimum bucket of 1 request per minute or allow deterministic sampling
- Model variant incompatibility (quantized vs full) — need compatibility check on creation of rollout

Ella: Non-goals (explicit):
- Not doing automatic model quality evaluation via user feedback for MVP
- Not building fine-grained UI for rollout analytics (console only shows summary in MVP)

Kevin: Security/compliance note: rollout API must respect customer isolation on Private deployments; control-plane calls should be tenant-scoped and audited. Add KMS check for any stored keys.

Maria: UX ask: include a simple 'preview' API to list the effective routing decision for a sample user_id — helps customers verify config.

Raj: Open questions to resolve in RFC:
1) Sampling determinism algorithm (hash of request id vs random)
2) Priority rules for conflicting rollouts
3) Acceptance hook schema (we need standard keys for latency/error/quality to wire into alerts)

Ella: Next steps: I'll draft a one-page PRD with problem statement, goals/non-goals, MVP acceptance criteria, and the three RFC questions. Engineers (Tess/Kevin) — please add feasibility notes inline by EOD Friday. Maria/Raj — add customer impact numbers & OKRs. ops-bot: add runbook link to PRD when ready.

Tess: Ack — will add feasibility with rough tasks.

Kevin: I'll scope observability and runbook items.

Maria: I'll share customer emails to quote the ask.

Ella: Thanks — aiming to have PRD + RFC draft for review next Tues. :thumbsup:
